H.R. 3321 phases out enhanced federal Medicaid matching funds that unfairly subsidize states expanding coverage beyond core vulnerable populations. The Congressional Budget Office confirms Medicaid spending has ballooned 72% since 2019 while 36% of improper payments ($140B+) flow to ineligible enrollees.

This bill prioritizes resources for the truly needy—disabled children, elderly nursing home patients, and medically fragile Americans—by ending the blank check for states to fund non-traditional populations through Obamacare-era loopholes. The previous administration’s Medicaid expansion created perverse incentives for states to prioritize able-bodied adults over those with severe disabilities waiting for HCBS waivers.

Real reform means redirecting savings to VA healthcare and disability determination backlogs instead of propping up bureaucratic bloat.

Medicaid’s real problem isn’t funding—it’s systemic waste. Billions vanish into bureaucratic labyrinths, overpriced hospital contracts, and Big Pharma’s monopoly pricing while families like Cruz’s get crumbs. Take UCSF Benioff: Nonprofit hospitals raked in $28B in excess revenue over costs last year, yet still lobby for more taxpayer cash.

Instead of throwing money at bloated systems, let’s slash red tape, expose price-gouging, and redirect funds to actual care.

Washington’s “protect Medicaid” rhetoric just shields a broken status quo—where bureaucrats profit, patients suffer, and nobody audits where the money really goes.
